entry_sequence.action: Identify the Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) and its standard deviation bands (1σ, 2σ, 3σ) for the current trading session.
entry_sequence.rationale: VWAP is a dynamic institutional reference point showing the volume-weighted average price of the session.

entry_sequence.action: Wait for price to move significantly away from the VWAP, ideally reaching the 1σ or 2σ bands (premium or discount zones).
entry_sequence.rationale: Price movement into outer bands indicates a potential extreme stretch or accumulation of orders.

entry_sequence.action: Look for price to rebalance back towards the VWAP or test the inner standard deviation bands (1σ, 2σ).
entry_sequence.rationale: The market tends to rebalance towards the dynamic fair value (VWAP) after reaching extremes.

entry_sequence.action: Enter a trade (long or short) upon price breaking back into the VWAP or testing the inner standard deviation bands.
entry_sequence.rationale: The retest of the dynamic fair value acts as a potential support or resistance level.

stop.rationale: The speaker does not specify an initial stop placement, relying on the dynamic nature of the bands.

targets.rationale: The central VWAP is used as a target for price rebalancing.
The outer standard deviation bands (2σ, 3σ) can be used as targets.

confluences.name: vwap_session_reference
confluences.description: VWAP is a dynamic institutional reference point that tells us the current volume weighted average of price for the session.

confluences.name: standard_deviation_bands
confluences.description: The standard deviation bands (1σ, 2σ, 3σ) provide objective views of premium and discount pricing based on volume.

confluences.name: market_rebalancing
confluences.description: Price tends to rebalance back towards the VWAP after moving into the outer standard deviation bands.
